overview.headline: Secret summer meeting in Philadelphia creates new frame of government

keyPoints.point: Delegates worked in secret during the summer to draft the new government document
keyPoints.quote: Drafted in secret by delegates to the Constitutional Convention during the summer of 1787

keyPoints.point: The Federal Convention convened in Philadelphia intending to revise the Articles of Confederation
keyPoints.quote: The Federal Convention convened in the State House (Independence Hall) in Philadelphia on May 14, 1787, to revise the Articles of Confederation.

keyPoints.point: Members adjourned day to day until a quorum of seven states was obtained because only two were present
keyPoints.quote: the members adjourned from day to day until a quorum of seven states was obtained on May 25.

keyPoints.point: By mid-June discussion made clear the Convention would draft an entirely new frame of government instead of amending
keyPoints.quote: rather than amend the existing Articles, the Convention would draft an entirely new frame of government.

keyTerms.gloss: minimum number of members needed for states to conduct business and make decisions
keyTerms.quote: the members adjourned from day to day until a quorum of seven states was obtained on May 25.

keyTerms.gloss: earlier agreement created for the states that the Convention gathered to revise
keyTerms.quote: The Federal Convention convened in the State House (Independence Hall) in Philadelphia on May 14, 1787, to revise the Articles of Confederation.

keyTerms.gloss: national level that holds power debated for balance with state interests
keyTerms.quote: Among the chief points at issue were how much power to allow the central government, how many representatives in Congress to allow each state

keyTerms.gloss: cooperative result shaped by many minds balancing different views with statesmanship
keyTerms.quote: The work of many minds, the Constitution stands as a model of cooperative statesmanship and the art of compromise.
